c.tagline: Africa's westernmost tip, where Atlantic surf meets vibrant city life.

taxi.fareNote: Most taxis lack working meters; negotiate the fare before departure. Tourist-rate taxis and app-based rides are more predictable.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing and aggressive vendors around Plateau, Sandaga market and the Corniche; caution at night

hood_desc: The historic administrative and business core on the southern peninsula tip, with colonial architecture, government buildings, the Place de l'Indépendance and Dakar's main museums; suits first-time visitors wanting to walk to sights and ferries to Gorée Island.

A quiet, leafy, upscale residential district near embassies and the Corniche, popular with expats and NGO workers; suits travelers wanting a calm, safe base with good restaurants a short taxi from downtown.
Dakar's trendiest coastal strip of restaurants, nightlife and beach clubs facing the Îles de la Madeleine; suits visitors who want a resort-like feel with easy beach and surf access.
A small fishing-village peninsula and popular surf beach right next to the airport road, with a laid-back, bohemian vibe; suits surfers, backpackers and those wanting sunset views over the bay.
A relaxed, artsy residential/beach neighborhood near Yoff beach and the airport, home to many guesthouses and yoga/surf retreats; suits budget travelers and long-stay digital nomads.
lodging: Radisson Blu Hotel Dakar Sea Plaza

water.note: Water is treated but aging pipes create contamination risk; most residents and visitors drink bottled water.

transit.pay: Sunu BRT and TER use contactless smart cards or mobile payment tapped at station gates; Dakar Dem Dikk buses and shared car rapide/Ndiaga Ndiaye minibuses are paid in cash to the conductor onboard.
transit.hours: Buses and BRT run roughly 6:00-22:00; TER operates approximately 5:30-22:30; limited night options rely on taxis or ride-hailing apps.
transit.note: The TER links Dakar to Diamniadio near the airport; the new electric Sunu BRT runs along a dedicated corridor from Petersen (Plateau) to Guédiawaye.

bus: Intercity coaches from Gare Routière Pompiers

transit.m: Shared taxi/car rapide to Diamniadio then onward transport

tip.r: Not obligatory but appreciated; rounding up or 5-10% at restaurants is common for good service.
